summary: This page of the SGX REIT annual report presents 2025 financial highlights, including a Distribution per Unit of 11.58¢ and Distributable Income of S\$860.9m, alongside portfolio metrics such as total property value of S\$27.4b and committed occupancy of 96.9%, along with capital management details like aggregate leverage at 38.6%. The section also covers green financing activities, sustainability ratings (including GRESB 5-Star), and recognition awards without containing audited portfolio statements, tenant tables, or explicit revenue/expense breakdowns.

This page presents the Financial Highlights for CICT Group, reporting Gross Revenue, Distributable Income, Net Property Income, and Total Assets in SGD million (or billion), alongside a comprehensive table of selected financial data including Distribution Per Unit, Management Expense Ratio, Aggregate Leverage, and Interest Coverage from 2021 to 2025. The reporting unit is SGD'000 for most line items and SGD'000,000 for Total Assets, with key metrics such as DPU rising from 10.40¢ to 11.58¢ and aggregate leverage fluctuating between 37.2% and 40.4%.

This page details ESG highlights and corporate governance metrics for CICTML, including employee training participation, volunteer hours, carbon reduction targets, board composition (67% independent), committee structures, and meeting attendance rates. No schema-relevant data such as audited portfolio statements, financial reports, tenant information, or distribution figures are present on this page.

This page details the trust structure of CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust (CICT), identifying the Manager as CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust Management Limited, the Trustee as HSBC Institutional Trust Services (Singapore) Limited, and listing three Property Managers: CapitaLand Retail Management Pte Ltd, CapitaLand Commercial Management Pte. Ltd., and Orchard Turn Developments Pte. Ltd. (OTD). It explicitly names properties managed by OTD including ION Orchard and ION Orchard Link, while noting that some international assets are managed by third-party providers in Germany and Australia; no audited Portfolio Statement, financial statements, revenue/expense notes, tenant mix tables, or distribution highlights are present on this page.

This page features portraits and titles for Chairman Teo Swee Lian and CEO Tan Choon Siang, alongside a Chairman and CEO Message highlighting FY 2025 performance with gross revenue of S$1,619.2 million (SGD'000), net property income of S$1,189.7 million, distributable income of S$860.9 million, and a distribution per unit (DPU) of 11.58 cents. The message explicitly names ION Orchard and CapitaSpring as key contributors but does not contain audited portfolio statements, detailed profit or loss breakdowns, top-N tenant tables, trade/tenant mix data, manager/trustee/sponsor info, or specific property-expense notes.

This page details the CICT Value Creation Strategy across four pillars and outlines significant capital movements including the divestment of 45% interest in CapitaSpring's SR component for S$280.0 million, the full divestment of Bukit Panjang Plaza for S$428.0 million, and the acquisition of a 55% interest in CapitaSpring's Commercial Component valued at S$1,900.0 million on a 100% basis. No audited Portfolio Statement, financial statements (profit or loss), gross revenue/expense notes, tenant mix tables, distribution highlights, or manager/trustee information are present on this page; therefore, no schema-relevant data is found.

This page presents an audited Portfolio Statement of property valuations as at 31 December 2025, reporting a total portfolio value of S$27.4 billion (S$ million) with a year-on-year increase of 5.2% driven by the acquisition of 55% interest in CapitaSpring and valuation uplifts for Gallileo and the Singapore portfolio. The statement details valuations across Retail, Office, and Integrated Development sectors, listing specific properties such as Bedok Mall, ION Orchard, and Raffles City Singapore, along with supporting notes on valuation drivers like rent improvements, occupancy changes, and currency conversions.

This page presents the audited portfolio statement showing total property valuations of S$27,397.5 million as at 31 December 2025, with a 5.2% increase driven by Singapore and Germany portfolios, while Australia declined due to currency depreciation and higher capitalisation rates. The report details specific asset valuations (e.g., Main Airport Center, Raffles City Singapore) using the income capitalisation method and discounted cash flow analysis conducted by multiple independent valuers.

This page presents gross revenue figures for FY 2025 totaling S$1,619.2 million (reported in millions of Singapore Dollars), detailing a breakdown by property category including Retail, Office, and Integrated Development with specific contributions from assets like Bedok Mall, CapitaSpring, and Raffles City Singapore, alongside notes on acquisitions such as the Glory Office Trust stake and divestments like 21 Collyer Quay.

This page presents financial highlights for SGX REIT, including a trade/tenant mix breakdown of Gross Revenue and Net Property Income (NPI) by segment in S$ million, distributable income figures totaling S$860.9 million with a DPU of 11.58 cents for the full year, and asset details showing total assets of S$27.4 billion as at 31 December 2025.

This page details CICT Group's financial derivatives, funding sources (52% Unsecured Bank Loans, 38% Medium Term Notes, 10% Secured Bank Loans), and interest rate sensitivity showing an estimated DPU decline of -0.35 cents for a 1% p.a. rate increase. It reports aggregate leverage at 38.6%, average debt cost at 3.2%, and confirms sufficient facilities to manage S\$651.0 million in borrowings maturing in 2026, with no audited Portfolio Statement, revenue/expense tables, tenant data, or distribution highlights present.

This page presents the Debt Maturity Profile as at 31 December 2025 in SGD million, detailing borrowings by year from 2026 to 2035 across Medium Term Notes (MTN), Secured Bank Loans, and Unsecured Bank Loans for CICT Group and its joint ventures. The report also provides liquidity information noting a cash balance of S$149.5 million as at that date, alongside disclosures on foreign exchange risk management and accounting policies under RAP 7.

This page details the 2025 trading performance of CICT's Units, reporting a total volume of 6.2 billion Units and an average daily volume of 24.6 million Units with unit prices ranging from S$1.91 to S$2.42, alongside a table of monthly volumes and prices. It also presents Total Unitholder Return figures for 1-year, 3-year, and 5-year periods (showing capital appreciation, distribution yields, and total returns) and a five-year comparison table covering opening/closing prices, market capitalisation, net asset value per Unit, and cumulative trading volumes, all denominated in SGD or units without a specific monetary scale note.

This page presents an operations review of CICT's portfolio, detailing committed occupancy levels and weighted average lease expiry (WALE) metrics for retail, office, and integrated development assets as of 31 December 2025. It includes a table of occupancy percentages by category and specific WALE figures in years for each asset class, alongside narrative updates on leasing activity, tenant retention rates, and recent divestitures or reclassifications such as CapitaSpring.

This page presents the Portfolio Lease Expiry Profile (%) for Retail, Office, and Hospitality sectors from 2026 to 2031 and beyond, alongside a Top-N tenants table listing the top 10 tenants contributing 16.0% of GRI as of December 2025. The data is reported in percentages with no explicit reporting unit (e.g., SGD'000) shown for the figures.

This page presents the Diversified Tenant Business Trade Mix, detailing the percentage distribution across ten categories including Banking (18.7%) and Food & Beverages (17.8%), with further breakdowns for Other Office Trades and Other Retail Trades. It also outlines the Tenure Profile as 13% freehold and 87% leasehold properties based on gross floor area, alongside a Sensitivity Analysis estimating rental income impacts of S$7.8 million per 0.5% occupancy variance and S$11.7 million per 10% rent rate variance for FY 2025.

This page details CICT's office portfolio performance in FY 2025, highlighting strong demand that drove 0.8 million sq ft of new and renewed leases across sectors like Banking, Distribution & Trading, and IT & Telecommunications, alongside a positive rent reversion of 6.6% for Singapore properties reaching S$10.95 psf. The content includes a table of new lease trade categories by country with square footage and percentages, an expiry profile table for Grade A buildings showing exiring lease percentages and monthly average gross rents for 2026 and 2027, but contains no audited Portfolio Statement, Total Return data, top-N tenants, or manager/trustee information.

This page details the property specifics and financial performance of Bedok Mall as at 31 December 2025, reporting gross revenue in S$ million alongside a valuation of S$827.0 million and GFA of 334,300 sq ft. It includes an audited portfolio statement for valuations and tenant counts, a top-N tenants list featuring Hanbaobao Pte. Ltd., NTUC Enterprise Co-Operative Ltd, and Uniqlo (Singapore) Pte. Ltd., and a trade mix table showing Food & Beverages at 38.3% and Beauty & Health at 18.3%.

This page presents property-specific data for Bugis Junction, including an audited portfolio statement with valuations of S\$1,141.0 million (2024) and S\$1,155.0 million (2025), gross revenue notes showing S\$83.7 million (2024) and S\$84.9 million (2025), a top-N tenants list featuring BHG, Cold Storage, and Nitori, and a detailed trade mix table reporting categories such as Food & Beverages at 32.1% and Fashion & Accessories at 14.4%. The reporting unit is SGD'000.

This page presents an audited Portfolio Statement for CQ @ Clarke Quay as of 31 December 2025, reporting a valuation of S$413 million, 60 tenants with 97.6% committed occupancy, and gross revenue of S$32.2 million (S\$'000). It includes major tenant names, property details such as the BCA Green Mark Gold PLUS rating, and tables detailing the lease expiry profile through 2031+ and the trade mix by category.

This page details the IMM Building, Singapore's largest outlet mall, presenting property valuations and gross revenue for 2024 and 2025 (in S$ million), alongside a top-N tenants list including Best Denki, Cold Storage, and Extra Space Jurong. It also includes trade/tenant mix data categorized by sector such as Food & Beverages and Warehouse, along with lease expiry profiles through 2031+ and specific property information like address and green rating.

This page details the ION Orchard property, an iconic mall in Singapore with a total valuation of S$3,697.0 million (100% basis) as at 31 December 2024 and gross revenue of S$23.6 million for that year, alongside key metrics including 945,400 sq ft GFA, ~280 tenants, and ~98% committed occupancy. The reporting unit is S\$ million for financial figures and sq ft for area measurements.

This page presents an audited Portfolio Statement for Junction 8, a shopping mall located at 9 Bishan Place, with financial data reported in S$ million and key metrics as of 31 December 2025. The statement includes gross revenue of S$62.8 million, property valuations of S$815.0 million, and trade/tenant mix details showing Food & Beverages accounts for 39.3% of the portfolio, alongside a list of major tenants such as Best Denki and BreadTalk Group.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement for Lot One Shoppers' Mall as of 31 December, reporting a valuation of S$564.0 million (2024) and S$584.0 million (2025), with gross revenue of S$46.5 million (2024) and S$47.2 million (2025). The report includes a top-N tenants table listing BreadTalk Group Pte Ltd, NTUC Enterprise Co-Operative Ltd, and Pertama Merchandising Pte Ltd, alongside trade mix data showing Food & Beverages at 34.5% and Beauty & Health at 16.1%, along with lease expiry profiles from 2026 to 2031+.

This page presents an audited Portfolio Statement for Tampines Mall, detailing property valuations of S$1,158.0 million (2025) and 507,300 sq ft GFA as at 31 December 2025, alongside gross revenue notes indicating S$82.8 million in total revenue. The report includes a Top-N tenants list featuring Golden Village Multiplex Pte Ltd, NTUC Enterprise Co-Operative Ltd, and Uniqlo (Singapore) Pte. Ltd., a trade mix breakdown showing Food & Beverages at 33.9%, and lease expiry profiles through 2031+.

This page details the Westgate shopping mall in Jurong Gateway, Singapore, presenting a portfolio statement as at 31 December 2025 with valuations (S$ million), gross revenue (S$ million), and property metrics including GFA, NLA, and occupancy rates. It explicitly lists major tenants, provides a trade mix breakdown by retail category, and includes lease expiry profile data from 2026 to 2031+, while noting that reporting units are in S$ million.

This page details the Bugis+ shopping mall, a property with an as-of-December 2024 valuation of S$359.0 million and gross revenue of S$63.4 million for the year ending December 2024 (S$65.7 million in 2025), alongside its major tenants including Golden Village Multiplex Pte Ltd, JD Sports Fashion Pte. Ltd., and Uniqlo (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. The content also provides trade mix data showing Food & Beverages accounts for 38.0% of total trades, along with lease expiry profiles from 2026 to 2031+.

This page details the Bukit Panjang Plaza asset, reporting a valuation of S$389.0 million and gross revenue of S$65.7 million as at 31 December 2025 (in millions). It includes an audited portfolio statement with key metrics such as GFA, NLA, tenant count, and occupancy rates, alongside a top-N tenants list, trade mix breakdown by category, lease expiry profile, and property-specific information including address, land tenure, and sale price.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement for Asia Square Tower 2 as of 31 December 2025, reporting a valuation of S$2,252.0 million, gross revenue of S$104.3 million, and a trade mix dominated by Banking, Insurance & Financial Services (41.1%). The property details include 916,900 sq ft of GFA with 70 tenants, while major tenants listed are KPMG Services Pte. Ltd., Mitsui Group, and Mizuho Bank, Ltd.

This page presents the audited portfolio statement for CapitaGreen as of 31 December 2025, reporting a valuation of S$1,718.0 million, gross revenue of S$97.9 million, and 70 tenants with 97.8% committed occupancy. It includes major tenant names (Lloyd's of London, Rakuten Asia, The Work Project Group), a trade mix breakdown by sector dominated by Banking, Insurance & Financial Services at 55.7%, property details including BCA Green Mark Platinum rating, and a lease expiry profile from 2026 to 2031+.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement for CapitaSpring as of 31 December 2025, reporting a valuation of S$1,900.0 million and gross revenue of S$72.7 million on a 100% basis following CICT's acquisition of the remaining 55% interest in August 2025. The content includes a table of major tenants (JPMorgan Chase Bank, Millennium Capital Management, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation), a detailed trade mix by industry with Banking leading at 61.1%, property information such as BCA Green Mark Platinum certification, and a lease expiry profile spanning 2026 to 2031+.

This page details the Capital Tower property, a 52-storey Grade A office building with $1,471.0 million valuation and S$79.8 million gross revenue as at 31 December 2025 (S$'000), reporting trade mix data showing Banking, Insurance & Financial Services as the largest segment at 41.3%. Major tenants include CapitaLand Investment Limited, GIC Private Limited, and TikTok Pte. Ltd., alongside a lease expiry profile indicating 58.5% of leases expire in 2031+.

This page details the CapitaSky Grade A property in Singapore's Tanjong Pagar district, reporting an audited portfolio valuation of S\$1,263.0 million and gross revenue of S\$73.6 million as at 31 December 2024 (S\$'000 basis implied by table units). It explicitly lists major tenants including Allianz Group and Equinix Asia Pacific, provides a comprehensive trade mix showing Banking, Insurance & Financial Services at 36.2%, and presents lease expiry profiles from 2026 to 2031+ alongside BCA Green Mark Platinum certification and joint venture ownership structure between CICT and COREF.

This page details the Six Battery Road property, reporting a valuation of S$1,623.0 million and gross revenue of S$71.1 million as at 31 December 2025, with trade mix dominated by Banking (44.3%) and Legal (16.5%). It lists major tenants including Ice Data Services Singapore, Mayer Brown, and Standard Chartered Bank, along with lease expiry profiles from 2026 to 2031+.

This page details the Gallileo property, a 38-storey Grade A commercial building in Frankfurt's Banking District, reporting an audited portfolio valuation of EUR270.9 million (S$383.2 million) and S$6.8 million gross revenue as at 31 December 2025, with committed occupancy at 97.7% and a trade mix dominated by Banking, Insurance & Financial Services at 97.2%. The SGX REIT holds a 94.9% joint venture interest, and the data is presented in SGD'000 or EUR million.

This page details the Main Airport Center (MAC) property in Frankfurt, presenting a Statement of Portfolio with valuations and gross revenue data for 2024 and 2025 reported in SGD'000s alongside NLA and occupancy metrics. It explicitly lists Major Tenants including Dell GmbH and Lufthansa AG, provides a Trade Mix table by sector, and includes lease expiry profiles and joint venture ownership details without containing audited financial statements or distribution highlights.

This page details the audited Portfolio Statement for 66 Goulburn Street, reporting property valuations in A$ and S$ (S$000), gross revenue of S$16.3 million (2024) and S$15.8 million (2025), and a trade mix dominated by Government (27.0%) and Legal (20.9%) sectors as of December 2025.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement for the 100 Arthur Street building as at 31 December 2024 and 2025, reporting valuations in SGD million (S$261.0m/242.6m), NLA, tenant count, committed occupancy, and gross revenue of S$13.5m/S$15.0m respectively. It also includes a Top-N tenants table listing three major tenants, a detailed trade mix by sector showing IT & Telecommunications at 26.1%, and lease expiry profiles through 2031+.

This page presents a Statement of Portfolio (property valuations) for the Funan development as at 31 December, reporting valuation in SGD millions and GFA/NLA in sq ft. It includes gross revenue notes ($ million), a Top-N tenants list, and trade/tenant mix details alongside lease expiry profiles, with all data presented in SGD'000 or equivalent units.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement for Plaza Singapura as of 31 December, reporting a valuation of S$1,443.0 million (2025) and S$1,441.0 million (2024), alongside gross revenue of S$93.2 million (2025) and S$93.7 million (2024). The document includes top-N tenants such as Cold Storage Singapore and Golden Village Multiplex, a detailed trade mix showing Food & Beverages at 29.2%, and a lease expiry profile indicating 49.8% expiring in 2026.

This page presents property valuations and operational metrics for The Atrium@Orchard, reporting gross revenue in S$ million alongside trade mix, tenant counts, and occupancy rates. No audited portfolio statement, total return, financial highlights, or top-N tenants table are present.

This page presents property valuations and gross revenue data for Raffles City Singapore as of 31 December 2025, reporting figures in S$ million with a valuation of S$3,434.0 million and gross revenue of S$251.8 million alongside occupancy rates and trade mix percentages. The content includes a top-N tenants table listing Accenture Pte. Ltd., the Economic Development Board, and RC Hotels (Pte) Ltd, detailed trade mix categories ranging from Hospitality & Leisure at 35.1% to Other Office at 2.2%, and lease expiry profiles through 2031+.

This page details the 101-103 Miller Street and Greenwood Plaza property, reporting a total NLA of 498,500 sq ft with 80 tenants (70 as at 31 December 2025), committed occupancy of 92.6%–92.8%, and gross revenue of S$24.7 million (2024) to S$22.3 million (2025). The data includes a trade mix table showing Banking, Insurance & Financial Services as the largest segment at 36.9%, major tenant names such as Allianz Australia Services Pty Limited, and property information indicating a 50/50 co-ownership between CICT and Mirvac with freehold tenure.

This page contains the table of contents for SGX REIT's Financial Statements, listing sections including the Statement of Total Return, Distribution Statement, and Portfolio Statement. No specific numerical data, tenant details, or financial figures are present to populate the required schema fields.

This page contains the Independent Auditor's Report to the Unitholders of CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust, confirming that the financial statements as at 31 December 2025 present fairly in accordance with RAP 7. The report explicitly lists the included statements (including the portfolio statement and consolidated statement of total return) but does not contain any audited data tables, tenant mix, or specific financial figures such as revenue, expenses, or distribution amounts; therefore, no schema-relevant data is present.

This page contains the Independent Auditor's Report highlighting the Key Audit Matter regarding the valuation of investment properties (referencing Note 5), noting a carrying amount of S$25,602 million as at 31 December 2025 for assets in Singapore, Australia, and Germany. The report details the auditor's procedures on external valuers' work, assumptions used (discount rates, terminal capitalisation rates), and confirms disclosures are adequate, but does not include audited Portfolio Statements, financial statements with revenue/expenses, tenant tables, or DPU highlights.

This page presents the Group and Trust Statements of Financial Position as at 31 December 2025, reporting total assets in SGD'000. Key financial highlights include a net asset value per unit attributable to Unitholders of $2.14 for the Group and $2.05 for the Trust, alongside detailed breakdowns of non-current assets such as investment properties and loans and borrowings.

This page presents the Statement of Total Return for the year ended 31 December 2025, reporting total return before tax of $958,604 and after tax of $951,424 in SGD'000. The statement details gross revenue of $1,619,174, property operating expenses, management fees (base and performance components), finance costs, fair-value changes on investment properties, and taxation, with final earnings per unit listed as basic 12.62 cents and diluted 12.60 cents.

This page presents the Distribution Statement for the SGX REIT year ended 31 December 2025, reporting in SGD'000. It details total return attributable to Unitholders of $937,287 and distributions paid totaling $750,125, resulting in a distribution per unit of 11.58 cents and an amount available for distribution at year-end of $360,545. The statement includes specific breakdowns in Note A for management fees ($51,997), trustee fees ($3,507), fair-value changes on investment properties ($(66,206)), and share of results from joint ventures ($(116,753)).

This page presents the Statements of Movements in Unitholders' Funds for the Group and Trust for the year ended 31 December 2025, reporting financial highlights including net assets at the beginning ($15,524,456 SGD'000) and end ($16,292,063 SGD'000) of the year, total return attributable to unitholders ($937,287 SGD'000), management fees paid ($19,651 SGD'000), and distributions to unitholders ($(750,125) SGD'000). The reporting unit is SGD'000.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement for SGX REIT as at 31 December 2025, detailing property valuations and net assets attributable to unitholders in SGD'000 across Singapore, Australia, Germany, and other jurisdictions. The report lists specific properties including retail malls (e.g., Tampines Mall, Bugis Junction) and office buildings (e.g., Asia Square Tower 2, Raffles City Singapore), noting their tenure, lease terms, locations, existing uses, carrying values for 2025 and 2024, percentage of total net assets, and ownership trusts or entities.

This page of the SGX REIT annual report (as at 31 December 2025) details the independent property valuers for Retail, Office, and Integrated Developments assets across Singapore, Australia, and Germany, noting that fair values are based on capitalisation and/or discounted cash flow methods with net changes recognised in the Statement of Total Return. It explicitly includes contingent rents recognised in the Statement of Total Return for 2025 at SGD'000 as $84,444,000.

This page presents the Statement of Cash Flows for the year ended 31 December 2025, reporting net cash used in financing activities of $(450,001) thousand and cash and cash equivalents at year-end of $149,489 thousand (SGD'000). Significant non-cash transactions include unit issuances to the Manager for management fees ($49,765,000) and acquisition fees related to Glory Office Trust ($8,550,000), along with a distribution reinvestment plan issuance of 59,828,333 units.

This page outlines accounting policies for plant and equipment, investment properties, assets held for sale, and foreign currency transactions within an SGX REIT's annual report. It specifies that depreciation is recognized in the Statement of Total Return on a straight-line basis, while changes in fair value for investment properties are also recorded in the Statement of Total Return; no schema-relevant data such as audited portfolio statements, financial highlights, or tenant tables are present.

This page outlines the accounting policies for financial instruments, detailing the recognition, classification, and subsequent measurement of non-derivative financial assets such as trade receivables, amortised cost assets, and equity investments at fair value through other comprehensive income. It specifies that interest income, foreign exchange gains/losses, impairment, and gains/losses on derecognition are recognised in the Statement of Total Return, with no reporting unit (e.g., SGD'000) or schema-relevant data like tenant tables or DPU figures present.

This page presents accounting policy notes regarding FRS 118 and other standards, alongside a detailed Plant and Equipment table for the Group and Trust entities covering costs, accumulated depreciation, and carrying amounts in SGD'000 as of 31 December 2025. No schema-relevant data such as audited portfolio statements, total return, revenue/expense breakdowns, tenant tables, or manager/trustee information is present on this page.

This page presents the Audited Portfolio Statement for investment properties, detailing movements in carrying amounts and fair values for both the Group and Trust between January 1, 2024, and December 31, 2025, reported in SGD'000. The statement includes a reconciliation table showing acquisitions, capital expenditure, fair value changes, disposals, and reclassifications, alongside notes on security pledges, fair value hierarchy (Level 3), and valuation techniques such as the capitalisation and discounted cash flow methods.

This page details the valuation techniques and significant unobservable inputs used for Level 3 fair value measurements of investment properties, including capitalisation rates and discount rates by region (Singapore, Australia, Germany) and property type (Retail, Integrated Developments, Office). No audited Portfolio Statement, financial highlights, tenant data, or reporting unit schema are present.

This page details significant unobservable inputs for investment property valuations, specifically terminal yield rates by region and asset class (Singapore Retail, Integrated Developments, Office; Germany Office; Australia Integrated Developments, Office), and presents a table of Subsidiaries assets including unquoted equity investments and loans to subsidiaries valued in SGD'000. The section concludes with a narrative describing the August 2025 acquisition of the remaining 55% stake in Glory Office Trust, which reclassified the Group's investment from "Joint ventures" to "Subsidiaries."

This page details the financial status of subsidiaries, including loans with interest rates ranging from 2.97% to 5.00%, impairment allowance movements totaling $389,063,000 (2025) and $368,561,000 (2024), and a list of 16 subsidiaries incorporated in Singapore, Germany, Luxembourg, or the British Virgin Islands with ownership interests between 94.9% and 100%. The reporting unit is SGD'000.

This page details the Group's investments in joint ventures as of 31 December 2025 and 2024, reporting investment values in SGD'000 where the Group held $1,047,801 (2025) and $1,271,190 (2024), while loans to these entities were nil (2025) and totaled $197,624 (2024). The report provides a trade/tenant mix via a table listing ownership interests in joint ventures such as Glory Office Trust and various Orchard Turn entities, along with notes on divestments, acquisitions, and the winding up of One George Street LLP.

This page presents a table summarizing the financial information of the Group's material joint ventures for the year ended 31 December 2025, reporting figures in SGD'000. It details gross revenue of $248,946, total return, other comprehensive income, and net assets, while explicitly listing specific expense components including depreciation, interest income/expense, and income tax. The statement tracks the carrying amount of interests from 1 January to 31 December 2025, noting distributions received, divestments, and capital commitments across OTH Group and immaterial joint ventures columns.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement (property valuations) for Joint Ventures, reporting Gross Revenue of $102,128k (GOT) and $46,761k (OTH) alongside Total Return, Other Comprehensive Income, and Net Assets at year-end. The financial highlights include detailed line items such as depreciation, interest income/expense, and income tax expense, with a total Group's share of joint ventures' capital commitment of $3,686k and a carrying amount of interest in joint ventures at 31 December 2024 of $1,271,190k.

This page contains notes on joint operations, equity investments at fair value (specifically CLCT and Sentral REIT), and financial derivatives, presenting data for the Group and Trust in SGD'000. The reporting unit is SGD'000.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement of financial instruments subject to enforceable master netting arrangements for the SGX REIT Group and Trust as of 31 December 2025 and 2024, detailing gross amounts, offsets in the Statement of Financial Position, and net amounts presented. The data is reported in SGD'000 and includes specific line items such as interest rate swaps and cross currency swaps for both financial assets and liabilities under Group and Trust categories.

This page details the Group's deferred tax assets and liabilities for the years ended 31 December 2025 and 2024, reported in SGD'000. It specifies that net deferred tax liabilities relate to taxable temporary differences from fair value changes of overseas investment properties held by the Group.

This page details the reclassification of assets and liabilities held for sale regarding the Bukit Panjang Plaza transaction, alongside a comprehensive breakdown of trade receivables, prepayments, and other receivables for both the Group and Trust. The reporting unit is SGD'000.

This page presents a table of Lease Liabilities for the Group and Trust with values in SGD'000, detailing current and non-current amounts for 2025 and 2024, alongside tables of expenses recognised in the Statement of Total Return and total cash outflows for leases. Additionally, it includes definitions for Hedging reserves, Foreign currency translation reserves, and Fair value reserves within the Unitholders' Funds section.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement for Non-Controlling Interests (NCI) related to 79RR LLP and other immaterial subsidiaries, reporting financial data in SGD'000. The summary table details the subsidiary's gross revenue of $74,805, total return of $54,785, net assets of $618,884, and cash flows from operating activities of $55,728, along with NCI ownership percentages of 30.0% in 79RR LLP and 5.1% in MAC entities and Gallileo Co.

This page details Non-Controlling Interests ("NCI") financial data for the SGX REIT reporting unit in SGD'000, including gross revenue of $73,596 and total return of $33,131 attributable to NCI of $8,094, alongside a table of units in issue showing 7,298,470 units at 1 January 2024 and 7,611,318 units issued by year-end.

This page presents financial highlights for SGX REIT, specifically detailing Gross Revenue (comprising rental, car park, and other income totaling $1,619,174k and $1,586,329k for 2025 and 2024 respectively), Property Operating Expenses ($429,425k and $432,851k), Interest and Other Income ($6,781k and $12,765k), and Investment Income from equity distributions ($9,083k and $9,381k). All figures are reported in SGD'000.

This page presents SGX REIT Notes 25 and 26 detailing Group finance costs of $314,704 (2025) and $345,394 (2024), alongside a tax reconciliation showing total return before tax of $958,604 (2025) and $935,319 (2024) with an effective deferred tax expense of $7,180 (2025) and $(6,458) (2024). All financial figures are reported in SGD'000 for the year ended 31 December 2025.

This page presents the Earnings Per Unit (DPU) financial highlights for the Group, reporting total return attributable to Unitholders and weighted average units in SGD'000 for 2025 and 2024. It also includes related party disclosures identifying CapitaLand entities as managers and trustees who receive management and trustee fees payable in the normal course of operations.

This page details significant related party transactions with the Manager for 2025 and 2024, including asset enhancement works, leasing expenses, rental income, and divestment fees in SGD'000. It also outlines the Group's capital management policies, compliance with aggregate leverage limits and interest coverage ratios under the CIS code, and the framework for credit risk arising from tenant or counterparty defaults.
